content:
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max's starting prices are US$100 higher than the previous generation, and Apple has simultaneously applied the price increase to its entire iPhone lineup, including models with completely unchanged specifications.

That means the starting price of the base iPhone 17 has increased from US$799 to US$899; the iPhone Air has also broken the four-digit mark for the first time, with a starting price of US$1,099.

Both the iPhone 17e and iPhone 16 have also increased in price by US$100. The iPhone 17e has gone from its old starting price of US$599 to the current US$699.

Of course, consumers may be put off by the fact that an iPhone model that has been on sale for a year with completely unchanged specifications has nonetheless seen a price increase.

However, Apple continues to make adjustments in response to changes in the market environment, such as rising component costs for memory and storage chips, and a price increase of "just" US$100 is actually lower than what some analysts had originally expected.

Below is the complete iPhone price list after the price increases:

  • iPhone 17e: 256GB version US$699
  • iPhone 16: 128GB version US$799
  • iPhone 17: 256GB version US$899
  • iPhone Air: 256GB version US$1,099
  • iPhone 18 Pro: 256GB version US$1,199
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: 256GB version US$1,299
  • iPhone Duo: 256GB version US$1,999

With the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 17 Pro has been discontinued. The base iPhone 17 is expected to be succeeded by the iPhone 17e in the spring of 2027.

Apple has adjusted its release schedule — only the high-end versions of the new models will be launched this autumn, while updates to the base model and Air are expected to be released between March and April next year.
